officialName: Biserica Ortodoxă «Nașterea Sfântului Ioan Botezătorul» din Cebza
address: Cebza nr. 156 (parish address), 307111 Cebza, oraș Ciacova, jud. Timiș
metalVisibleInPhotos: No photos saved: no public photo of the parish church was found and the building is not located on the map.
verificationNotes: The Mitropolia Banatului list (Protopopiatul Deta) gives the Cebza parish church as «Nașterea Sf. Ioan Botezătorul», 1923, parish address nr. 156; ro.wikipedia instead says the village's Orthodox church was built in 1880 and survived the 1912 flood (date conflict). The other church in the village territory is the 1758 wooden church «Sf. Gheorghe» (LMI TM-II-m-A-06195) in the cemetery. It belongs to Mănăstirea Cebza (OSM node 487686311, about 0.7 km north), a monastery rather than the parish. The parish church is not mapped in OSM and could not be pinned down on imagery, so lat/lon = village centre. No news about the 2019 copper works was found (web search budget exhausted).

Racovița village has two churches. Wikimedia Commons (2009 photos) shows a white single-tower Banat-baroque church (category 'Romanian Orthodox Church in Racovița, Timiș') and a three-tower church with 1930 on the façade (category 'Church of the Nativity of Virgin Mary in Racovița', filed under Greek Catholic churches). The Orthodox deanery list (Protopopiatul Lugoj) gives the Racovița parish church as «Nașterea Maicii Domnului», 1930, which conflicts with the Commons classification. Neither church is mapped in OSM. Esri imagery (16 Oct 2019, before the 2021 order) shows a church with a bright metal roof and a west tower near 45.7007, 21.6398. No source ties the 2021 elZinc order to either building, so this stays UNRESOLVED. lat/lon = village centre.

heightHints: Single west-front bell tower with clock, a lantern and a cross over a gabled nave (2012 photo); no measured height.
metalVisibleInPhotos: 01.jpg (Commons, April 2012) predates the 2022 works. It shows the west front with the tower helm and lantern in light-grey sheet metal; the nave roof is hidden by trees. The new elZinc natural covering is not shown.
verificationNotes: Both point to the Orthodox parish church. The Mitropolia Banatului list (Protopopiatul Lugoj) gives the Balinț church as «Învierea Domnului», 1890. OSM node 2424275140 (place_of_worship, orthodox) sits on a church-shaped building with an apse on Esri imagery, in the village core. There is no OSM outline, so footprint = null. Two other OSM 'Biserica' Orthodox nodes lie about 2.3 km east and west of the centre, outside the village core. Historically the village also had Reformed, Greek-Catholic and Roman-Catholic believers (1910), but in 2002 490 of 614 inhabitants were Orthodox. No news about the 2022 works was found (web search budget exhausted).

Bobda has three churches. The Orthodox «Sf. Ev. Luca» (1864 per Protopopiatul Timișoara I; hu.wikipedia gives 1862). A Roman-Catholic church of 1876 (hu.wikipedia). The Csávossy mausoleum-church (Roman-Catholic, 1908, listed monument, OSM way 1120572241). Nothing distinguishes between the Orthodox and the 1876 Catholic church, so this stays UNRESOLVED. lat/lon = village centre.

metalVisibleInPhotos: 01.jpg (Commons, May 2026, side view): the tower roof, onion lantern and spire are clad in brown, matte sheet metal consistent with weathered copper (the 2023 order). The nave roof is red ceramic tile with solar panels.
verificationNotes: The village has the Orthodox church «Sf. Arh. Mihail și Gavriil» (1987; Protopopiatul Sânnicolau Mare, parish nr. 160) and the historic Swabian Roman-Catholic church (OSM node 12900464401, main road). A May 2026 Commons photo of the Catholic church shows red roofs and a red spire, so no copper there. The May 2026 photo of the Orthodox church shows the tower helm, lantern and spire in brown weathered metal, consistent with copper sheet and strip. That makes the Orthodox church the probable recipient, but no source confirms it. The church is not mapped in OSM and was not located on imagery, so lat/lon = village centre.

Hitiaș has two churches per ro.wikipedia: the Orthodox «Învierea Domnului» (1901; Protopopiatul Lugoj) and a Greek-Catholic church. Commons has only 2009 photos of the Orthodox church. Neither is mapped in OSM. A towered church is visible on Esri imagery near 45.7105, 21.5975 (denomination not determined). No source ties the 2023 order to either church, so this stays UNRESOLVED. lat/lon = village centre.
